<header class="c-pagehead">
  <div class="c-wrap">

    <h1>Public Health &amp; Informatics</h1>
    <p>
      Population data, read for burden and inequity. We study how disease is
      distributed in Bangladesh and South Asia, and whether the systems meant to
      address it actually reach the people who need them.
    </p>
  </div>
</header>

<section class="c-slab c-slab--paper">
  <div class="c-wrap">
    <div class="c-split">
      <div class="c-prose">

        <h2>Epidemiological surveillance</h2>
        <p>
          Observational study design and secondary analysis of national health
          surveys, used to quantify the burden of non-communicable disease and of
          infectious illness — and to say honestly how uncertain those estimates
          are in a setting with incomplete registration.
        </p>

        <h2>Digital health &amp; health systems</h2>
        <p>
          Evaluation of digital health interventions, electronic medical records
          and telemedicine: what they change in patient outcomes, and what they
          change in clinical workflow, which is often not the same thing.
        </p>

        <h2>Evidence synthesis for policy</h2>
        <p>
          Systematic reviews, meta-analyses and health economic modelling, produced
          to a standard that lets them be used in policy argument rather than only
          in academic argument.
        </p>

        <h2>Maternal &amp; child health</h2>
        <p>
          Social and environmental determinants of maternal outcomes and early
          childhood development, with attention to the gradients that national
          averages conceal.
        </p>
